established_claims.claim: The OBS-04 all-restore-MISS gate cannot fire under bundle drift.
established_claims.evidence: Gate is `readMisses === hashes.length && mirrored === 0` (publish-mirror.ts:804); a single restore hit breaks both conjuncts. Two artifacts, only one can drift: start-cache-server/action.yml has main: 'index.js' (the COMMITTED bundle, used by the sidecar jobs); packages/github-cache/action.yml has main: 'dist/action/index.js' (a build output, untracked -- `git ls-files packages/github-cache/dist` is empty -- rebuilt in-job at ci.yml:2367, so it CANNOT be stale). Both publish steps are `uses: ./packages/github-cache`, same job, so the seed's write version and publish's restore version are identical by construction.

established_claims.claim: ROBUST-04's surfacing sentence was FALSE WHEN WRITTEN, not invalidated by a later phase.
established_claims.status: CONFIRMED by the evidence auditor, including the check the orchestrator skipped
established_claims.evidence: 969de3e (the clause) = 2026-07-26. 80fb65f (operation: seed already in the publish job) = 2026-07-20, SIX DAYS EARLIER. The auditor did NOT trust the orchestrator's filtered rg view: it extracted the whole ci.yml at both commits, found a DECOY `operation: seed` in the standalone dogfood-seed job, and confirmed a SECOND one inside `publish:` between `npm run build` and `operation: publish`. It also checked the state at 969de3e itself, which the orchestrator never did.

refuted_claims.claim: The gap is now closed / drift is now surfaced by the proportional branch.
refuted_claims.refutation_1: Integrity critic: the proportional warning names exactly two candidate causes -- '(1) a cache-version rotation in this commit range ... (2) the runtime token's Actions-cache read scope' (publish-mirror.ts:895-902). Bundle drift is NEITHER, and the comment at :866 says 'Treat this branch as the live rotation signal.' So under drift a warning fires telling the reader to look for a rotation -- which IS the hazard ROBUST-04 described, relocated one branch over. VERIFIED DIRECTLY by the orchestrator.
refuted_claims.refutation_2: Evidence auditor, independently and more damagingly: the INPUT was wrong. 'Everything misses except the run's own seeds' ignores D3's membership-before-restore skip at line 635 -- an entry already in the shard is skipped with NO restore attempt, counted into alreadyPresent, NOT readMisses. It stays in the denominator and leaves the numerator. On the measured composition of run 31305961054 that gives ubuntu ~52/112 = 46%, wilsonLowerBound(52,112) = 0.3746, SILENT. Windows is worse.
refuted_claims.further: The outcome is ENUMERATION-ORDER dependent and order is pinned nowhere -- listCacheEntries passes only { owner, repo, ref, per_page }. Seed-early means maximal already-present skipping and silence; seed-last means 111/112 and a warning. The only case where the warning reliably fires is month-shard rollover, when the shard is empty.

refuted_claims.claim: 'The mirror silently stops receiving anything' is simply TRUE.
refuted_claims.refutation: TRUE WITH A CAVEAT. The shard still receives the publish leg's own seed -- that upload is the same event C1 uses to prove the gate stays silent, so a correction cannot assert both 'receives nothing' and 'the seed mirrors'. Substantively right (no real task content reaches the shard), literally false. Reword to 'stops receiving real cache content' or 'receives only its own synthetic seed'.

refuted_claims.claim: The small-N residual is theoretical because a consumer has no second artifact to drift against.
refuted_claims.refutation: Conclusion right, REASON wrong. A consumer cannot run publishMirror AT ALL: packages/github-cache/package.json `files` carries '!dist/action', src/index.ts exports only createCacheServer, and the internal action.yml's main points at an untracked path so a `uses:` against the git ref cannot resolve it. The hole is UNREACHABLE for consumers, not merely theoretical. The version-mismatch CLASS is still reachable for them by other means (two jobs pinning different refs, a stale major tag) but surfaces as ordinary Nx misses, never as a publish warning.
